                    ### Question

This is her 4th visit for these symptoms in the last 5 years. She tells you she recently ran out of her normal "controller" medication. Concerned for an asthma exacerbation, you begin therapy with a short-acting beta2-agonist. What is the expected cellular response to your therapy?

                    ### Options

opc. Gq protein coupled receptor activates phospholipase C and increases intracellular calcium

ope. Gi protein coupled receptor inhibits adenylyl cyclase and decreases cAMP

This results in bronchodilation. The evidence paths support the role of adenylyl cyclase in increasing cAMP levels, aligning with the consensus mechanism of action.
